exposure: Surgical care provided by general practitioners with 12 months of surgical training and certified by a 'Capacity of District Surgery' diploma
Surgical care provided by general practitioners (GP) who received 12-month training in surgery, certified by a 'Capacity of District Surgery' (CDS) diploma
outcome: Proportion of emergency vs. elective surgeries
Number of patients transferred to a higher-level facility
cohort: Patients undergoing surgical procedures at 21 district hospitals in an unspecified country
finding: District surgery, performed by trained general practitioners, effectively addressed the shortage of skilled medical personnel for basic emergency and elective surgeries in rural areas.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the most common emergency surgical procedure (37.21%), and 102 deaths (2.87% of all deaths) occurred following cesarean section.
